root.name: English Opening: Anglo-Dutch Variation, Chabanon Gambit

overview: After 1.c4 f5 2.Nf3 d6 White plays 3.e4, a Chabanon-style pawn offer. If Black takes on e4, White develops with Nc3 or Ng5 and aims at e4 and f7 for compensation. The closely related Ferenc Gambit (2.Nc3 Nf6 3.e4) is the most played line in the surrounding subtree, so this page often shows it.

white_ideas.idea: Offer the e4 pawn and win time with Ng5 or Nc3
Take the centre with d4 after the pawn is accepted
Attack f7 with Ng5, Qh5+ or Bc4

black_ideas.idea: Take on e4 and consolidate with ...Nf6 and ...e5

typical_structures.structure: White centre with c4 and d4 against Black f5-d6 set-up
Open e-file after the exchange on e4

character.notes: Gambit play with tactics around e4 and f7, and a risky king for Black.

gambit.notes: Black can accept on e4 and keep the pawn if able to meet the pressure on e4 and f7.

soundness.notes: Plausible compensation but not proved; treated as fine for a surprise attempt.

structure.notes: The centre opens after fxe4, giving pieces active play.

approach.notes: Gambits against the Dutch are seldom chosen by strong players.

level.notes: Need to know the typical tactics and when to take the pawn back.

sublines_that_differ.name: Ferenc Gambit
sublines_that_differ.how: Different move order, most played in the subtree; same idea.

character.reason: A pawn gambit against Black king with tactics around e4 and f7.

gambit.reason: White offers the e4 pawn for development.

soundness.reason: Compensation is plausible and nobody calls it refuted.

structure.reason: The e4 exchange opens the centre for the pieces.

level.reason: The plan is clear but sound handling needs judgement.

plans.reason: White pays a pawn for development and pressure on f7.
